text:
ConocoPhillips stock fell 0.6% today and is down 9.6% over two weeks, tracking a sharp decline in oil prices. US crude has slipped to $99.64 a barrel from the $154 range at the start of this period—a drop of more than 35%—which directly cuts into the earnings power of oil producers like ConocoPhillips. The company reported quarterly results on November 5th, but the broader pressure from falling crude prices appears to have overwhelmed any company-specific positives.

The stock's recent weakness also reflects a shift in the political landscape. Democrats swept the midterm elections, and one outcome is a likely stronger push toward renewable energy and climate policies less favorable to traditional oil companies. At the same time, geopolitical risk in the Middle East remains a live threat—which would normally support oil prices—but it hasn't been enough to offset the fundamental decline in crude since late October.
